name: Trinidad (Cuba)
tagline: Sugar-era colonial town of cobbles and salsa
summary: Trinidad is a perfectly preserved colonial town built on 19th-century sugar wealth, with pastel houses on cobbled streets. Hear live son and salsa on the Casa de la Música steps, ride the steam train or horses through the Valle de los Ingenios sugar valley, swim at Playa Ancón and hike to waterfalls in Topes de Collantes.
seasonNote: Dry season December to April; hurricane season June to November.
arrival: About 4 hours by Víazul bus or car from Havana or Cienfuegos (1.5 hours).
gettingAround: Walk the old town; taxis, bikes or horses for the valley and beach.
cashTip: Bring cash (euros or US dollars); foreign cards often fail. Prices here are in US dollars; tip 10 percent.
foodTip: Ropa vieja, lobster in casas particulares and canchánchara (rum, honey and lime).
buyTip: Embroidered linen and cigars (from official shops).
baseArea: A casa particular in the old town
